papers.title_in_file: Entropy Computing: A photonics-enabled quantum computing solution for optimization (Photonic Integrated Circuits Magazine, 16 March 2026, by Jenn Robinson, Lac Nguyen, Pouya Dianat and Yong Meng Sua, QCi)
papers.version_note: A browser print of a PIC Magazine web article (printed 4/14/26). All six pages are images, so the text is OCR text; the text layer is empty. It is the trade-magazine summary of Nguyen et al., Communications Physics 8, 411 (2025), not that paper. Page 1 is the magazine cover and page 6 is a list of related-article thumbnails. Some lines on pages 3, 4 and 5 are garbled by the OCR where a sticky site header or banner overlaps the text; those lines were read from the page images.
sections_read: QCi foundry and the quantum supply chain of the future (p.5)

figures.shows: Cover of Photonic Integrated Circuits magazine, issue 1 2026, headline about co-packaged optics in optical testing; a technician at an optical test bench. It carries no content about entropy computing.
A rack-mount silver instrument chassis with a perforated front panel; the caption names it as QCi's Dirac-3 hybrid photonic system. No data are shown.
figures.confirmed_by: QCi's Dirac-3 hybrid photonic system uses entropy computing to tackle complex NP-hard optimization problems

figures.shows: Panel a: schematic of the Dirac-3 loop. A pump laser feeds a variable optical attenuator (VOA) and an electro-optic modulator (EOM) driven by a DAC; a Hamiltonian encoder and an FPGA do the feedback calculation and a mean photon number controller; light is combined at a coupler with unmodulated light and goes through a PPLN crystal to a single photon detector; a time-correlated photon counter records single photon arrival times against a reference clock T; vacuum noise enters at the detector. Electrical and optical signals are colour-coded. Panel b: encoding with amplitude: time-bin variables V1 to Vn, a linear loss mapping C1 to Cn, and wavefunction creation, with the state written as a sum of Ci times Vi and the squared coefficients summing to 1. Panel c: decoding from single photon accumulations: wavefunction collapse in each clock cycle, detected photons counted per time bin over N loops, giving a state vector such as [3, 6, 1, 3, ..., 2, 4].

figures.shows: Panels a to c: drawings of a 30-node graph cut into 2, 3 and 4 groups (max-2-cut, max-3-cut, max-4-cut). Panels d to l: histograms of frequency (y, axis ticks 0 and 30) against cut size (x) for each case, in three rows: EQC schedule 1 (red), EQC schedule 4 (green) and SDP (blue). x axis ticks run about 120 to 150 for max-2-cut, about 150 to 190 for max-3-cut and about 160 to 200 for max-4-cut. In max-3-cut and max-4-cut the EQC histograms are narrow and sit at the upper end of the range, and the SDP histograms are wide and low. In max-2-cut the EQC schedule 4 histogram has its tallest bar at the upper end, near about 150.
figures.confirmed_by: A 30-node unweighted graph was considered, which was then cut into a varying number of subsets.

figures.shows: Thumbnails of related news articles (the Dirac-3 chassis, a micro-LED interconnect, a Uviquity chip, a photonic chip, a bioreactor sensor). No data on entropy computing.

papers.what_it_is: A vendor-authored trade-magazine article in which QCi staff summarize their Dirac-3 entropy computing machine and its optimization benchmarks, citing a 2025 Communications Physics paper, and describe the QCi foundry.
